title: Samples Dojo - weekly sketches and standup notes (Mar 03 2026)
content:
Context and purpose:
This is a lightweight weekly sketch for the Samples Dojo workstream — focused on SDK-first sample apps, quickstarts, and the playground-in-a-box initiative. Use as the running notes for our Thu standup and as a handoff doc for on-call / rotation folks. Not a polished PRD, more of a scratchpad with action items and followups.

Attendees (quick):
- Aisha B. (owner)
- Marco L. (samples infra)
- Priya R. (docs + quickstarts)
- Jonas E. (QA / e2e)
- Maya O. (developer advocacy)

TL;DR updates this week:
- Quickstart completion funnel up: demo completions 42 -> 58 week-over-week after the new onboarding flow landed in the TS quickstart.
- Go SDK: hotfix merged to fix streaming reconnect when network flaps (PR 412). Need backport to 0.9.x.
- Playground-in-a-box: prototype v0.2 shipped to staging, but GH Actions e2e is flaky on macOS runners. Investigation assigned.
- Samples repo restructure (split /recipes) still WIP; blocked on CI config (circle -> GH actions) and package publishing policy.

Notes / detailed items:
1) Quickstarts and docs
- Priya: updated the text quickstart for embeddings to include a small counterexample showing different vector normalization behaviors across model families (very useful for customers). Left TODO to add a short snippet comparing Redwood-verified models vs. upstream open checkpoints.
- Observed friction: the modal that prompts to create API keys in the hosted demo is confusing; several users drop at call-to-action. Maya to sketch alternative microcopy + flow.
- Metric: quickstart-to-first-call conversion: 14% -> 19% (tracked in console). Still want 30%+ eventual target for first-time users.

2) SDKs and sample apps
- Marco: Go SDK reconnect fix (PR 412) merged to main. Backport plan: cut patch branch 0.9.x, apply fix, run regression suite. Target: ship patch by Mon 2026-03-08.
- TS SDK: intermittent flakiness in unit tests that rely on setTimeout and fake timers — appears when run under GH Actions matrix with node 20. Jonas to add flaky test tag and open issue for maintainers.
- Python sample: added a short demo showing caching + prompt templates; needs a short video recorded for the quickstart page. Action: Aisha to record (5-7 min) by next Thu.

3) Playground-in-a-box (local dev experience for customers)
- What shipped in v0.2: single-binary dev mode, example dataset loader, preconfigured model presets. Works locally on Linux.
- macOS runners fail intermittently on GH Actions due to Docker for Mac permission edge-case — workaround is to use podman or run inside a Linux VM. Not acceptable for customers.
- Action: Marco + Jonas to pair and create a reproducible GH Actions job that fails in CI; file infra ticket (RI-1254) to request infra team's help to repro on our private runners.

4) Samples repository restructure
- Goal: split large monolithic /samples into smaller, focused packages (/recipes, /examples, /cli-helpers) to make release cycles independent.
- Blocker: package publishing policy (npm org and PyPI name collisions). Legal/Registry check pending.
- Action: Priya to draft a proposed layout + publish plan and share with platform-eng for review by Fri 2026-03-06.

5) Observability + metrics for samples
- Added lightweight event hooks for quickstart completion and demo abandonment. These emit a minimal payload to console-telemetry for now.
- Need to add tokenized usage estimates (approx cost per quickstart run) to the cost-preview UI inside the quickstart modal. Aisha to propose copy and a simple cost calc by next week.

6) Bugs / incidents this week
- Incident: e2e GH Actions matrix failing on macOS for the playground job. Severity: P2 — user-facing for customers trying local builds on Macs. Temporary workaround doc added.
- Incident: One report of the TS samples not handling 302 redirects from proxy when using local tunnels. Root cause suspected in node-fetch behavior. Jonas to add a failing test and a repro case.

Open questions / things to decide
- Do we default quickstarts to the lowest-latency model in the catalog or the smallest-cost model? Tradeoffs: latency-first gives better UX on demo, cost-first aligns with Redwood Optimize messaging. Need product call.
- How aggressive should backports be for SDK patches? We have limited eng capacity and a couple of customers on 0.9.x. Proposal: severe bug -> backport; otherwise target next minor. Vote in comments.

Action items (owners + due dates)
- Marco: backport Go SDK reconnect fix to 0.9.x, run regression -> due 2026-03-08.
- Priya: publish plan for samples repo split and legal registry check -> due 2026-03-06.
- Jonas + Marco: reproduce GH Actions macOS failure and file infra ticket (RI-1254) -> due 2026-03-05.
- Aisha: record Python sample quickstart video and draft cost-preview copy -> due 2026-03-10.
- Maya: new microcopy + flow sketch for API key modal -> due 2026-03-09.

Notes to self / scratchpad
- Consider adding a tiny interactive diff in quickstarts to show how prompt edits change token counts in real-time. Could be a follow-up enhancement.
- Look into adding a "repro script" template for customers to file bugs easily (one shell script that grabs logs + minimal environment).

Next sync
- Thu standup next week: 2026-03-12 09:30 PT (tentative). Will run 15 minutes, same quick format: 60s updates / 30s blockers / 5m triage.

References / links (scratch):
- PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/samples/pull/412
- Jira: RI-1254 (playground macOS CI fail)
- Slack: #devx-samples (pinned: quickstart-funnels, GH actions failures)

If anything missing or clearly wrong, ping me in Slack or edit this doc.

-- Aisha
